To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the dynamic programming can be done inO(n log log n) time, and (2) the dynamic programming is a good approach to solve the dominating set problem on a class of graphs, and it is worth the time to find the best way to implement it.

the minimum cardinality dominating set problem on a permutation graph can be solved inO(n log log n) time, and the minimum weight dominating set problem on the same graph can be solvedO(n2 log2 n) time.
the dominating set problem can be solved on permutation graphs inO(n log log n) (resp. O(n2 log2 n)) time, assuming the input graph is given as a permutation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two questions.
the design of efficient algorithms for the dominating set problem on the permutation graph class.
the design and analysis of efficient data structures and fast algorithms for permutation graphs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dominating set problem on permutations can be solved inO(n log log n) time.
our new algorithm is the fastest algorithm to solve the minimum dominating set problem on general graphs.
our algorithm is the best-known algorithm for the minimum cardinality and weight dominating set problem on the class of permutation graphs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dynamic programming is not the best way to solve the dominating set problem on a special class of graphs.
the minimum cardinality dominating set problem on general graphs is solved inO(n3), and on permutation graphs inO(n2 log2 n).
we have reduced the time complexity by a factor ofO(logn (resp.O(log2n)) in both the minimum cardinality and the minimum weight cases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of dynamic programming in solving graph problems is often not the best approach, especially when the problem is on a restricted class of graphs.
the use of efficient data structures can lead to significant improvements in the running time.
the dynamic programming formulation of the dominating set problem is more amenable to improvement than previously thought.
